Linear equations and inequalities

How many hours do I have to work in my part-time job to pay for my driving licence? From how many items on is the machine worth it? How long do two pumps take together? Behind such questions there are equations and inequalities. In this chapter you solve them confidently, state the solution set correctly and recognise false solutions.

6 LESSONS3 UNITSNUMBER LINEWITHOUT AIDS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • solve linear equations with equivalence transformations and state the solution set, in the special cases too
  • solve linear inequalities and know when the sign is reversed
  • show solution sets on the number line and in set notation
  • solve equations with fractions that lead to linear equations, and sort out false solutions

Solve $2x + 3 = 13$.

$2x = 10$, $x = 5$

What is the lowest common denominator of $\tfrac14$ and $\tfrac16$?

$12$

What is $-3 \cdot (x - 2)$?

Multiply both terms by $-3$.

Which statement is true?

$-5$ lies further to the left on the number line.

UNIT 12 LESSONS

1Linear equations and their solution set

“I think of a number, multiply it by 3, subtract 7 and get 20.” As an equation: $3x - 7 = 20$. Thinking backwards: first add 7, then divide by 3. So $3x = 27$ and $x = 9$.

Every step changes both sides in the same way, so the equation stays in balance like a pair of scales. Such steps are called equivalence transformations: they do not change the solution set.

KEY POINT · EQUIVALENCE TRANSFORMATIONS AND SOLUTION SET

You may add or subtract the same number (or the same term) on both sides, and multiply or divide both sides by the same number $\neq 0$.

The solution set $L$ contains all numbers from the underlying set $G$ that satisfy the equation. Usually $G = \mathbb{R}$.

Special cases: at the end there is a contradiction such as $0 = 5$: $L = \{\,\}$. At the end there is a true statement such as $0 = 0$: $L = \mathbb{R}$.

The check: substitute the solution into the original equation. Both sides must have the same value.

Mind the underlying set: $2x = 3$ has the solution $1.5$ in $\mathbb{R}$, but none in $\mathbb{N}$.

INTERACTIVE · THE SCALES

Type the transformation applied to both sides, for example $-3$, $:4$ or $-2x$. Goal: $x$ on its own on one side.

EXAMPLE 1 · WITH BRACKETS

Solve $5(x - 2) - 3 = 2x + 8$ and check.

$5x - 10 - 3 = 2x + 8 \;\Rightarrow\; 5x - 13 = 2x + 8 \;\big|\; -2x + 13 \;\Rightarrow\; 3x = 21 \;\big|\; :3$, so $x = 7$.

Check: left $5 \cdot 5 - 3 = 22$, right $14 + 8 = 22$. $L = \{7\}$

EXAMPLE 2 · THE SPECIAL CASES

Solve a) $2(x + 3) = 2x + 6$   b) $4x - 1 = 4(x + 1)$.

a) $2x + 6 = 2x + 6 \;\big|\; -2x \Rightarrow 6 = 6$: always true, $L = \mathbb{R}$.

b) $4x - 1 = 4x + 4 \;\big|\; -4x \Rightarrow -1 = 4$: contradiction, $L = \{\,\}$.

EXERCISES

Solve: a) $4x + 7 = 31$   b) $12 - 3x = 0$   c) $\tfrac{x}{5} + 2 = 6$   d) $7x - 4 = 3x + 8$

a) $x = 6$   b) $x = 4$   c) $x = 20$   d) $4x = 12$, $x = 3$

Solve $2x + 9 = 4$ once with the underlying set $\mathbb{N}$ and once with $\mathbb{Q}$.

$2x = -5$, $x = -2.5$. In $\mathbb{N}$: $L = \{\,\}$. In $\mathbb{Q}$: $L = \{-2.5\}$.

Solve: a) $3(2x - 1) - 2(x + 4) = 5$   b) $(x + 2)^2 - x^2 = 16$

For b), apply the binomial formula. The $x^2$ then drops out.

a) $6x - 3 - 2x - 8 = 5 \Rightarrow 4x = 16 \Rightarrow x = 4$   b) $x^2 + 4x + 4 - x^2 = 16 \Rightarrow 4x = 12 \Rightarrow x = 3$

State the solution set: a) $3(x - 1) = 3x - 3$   b) $2x + 5 = 2(x + 3)$   c) $0.5(4x - 2) = 2x - 1$

a) $L = \mathbb{R}$   b) $5 = 6$: $L = \{\,\}$   c) $2x - 1 = 2x - 1$: $L = \mathbb{R}$

Explain the trick “Always five” from the explorations with a term. Invent a trick of your own that always gives 7.

$\tfrac{2x + 10}{2} - x = x + 5 - x = 5$, whatever $x$ is. Your own trick, for example: triple it, add 21, divide by 3, subtract the number: $\tfrac{3x + 21}{3} - x = 7$.

TEST YOURSELF!

Solve $5(x - 2) - 3 = 2x + 8$.

$3x = 21$, $x = 7$

What is the solution set of $4x - 1 = 4(x + 1)$?

What remains is $-1 = 4$, a contradiction.

Solve $\tfrac{x}{5} + 2 = 6$.

$\tfrac{x}{5} = 4$, $x = 20$

UNIT 22 LESSONS

2Linear inequalities

For the driving licence from the exploration, $2400 - 900 = 1500$ euros are missing. At €12.50 an hour we need $12.5\,x \geq 1500$, so $x \geq 120$. The answer is not a single number but all numbers from 120 on: the solution set is a half-line.

Inequalities are solved almost like equations. Only one transformation is tricky: multiplying $2 < 5$ by $-1$ gives $-2 > -5$. When you multiply or divide by a negative number, the order on the number line is reversed.

KEY POINT · LINEAR INEQUALITIES

Adding and subtracting on both sides and multiplying and dividing by a positive number do not change the sign.

When you multiply or divide by a negative number, the sign is reversed: $<$ becomes $>$, $\leq$ becomes $\geq$.

Solution set: $L = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x \geq 120 \,\}$. On the number line a half-line, the end point filled for $\leq$ and $\geq$, open for $<$ and $>$.

Double inequality: $3 \leq 2x - 1 < 9$ is transformed in all three parts at once: $2 \leq x < 5$.

Check with a test number: choose a number from the solution set and one outside it and substitute both.

INTERACTIVE · INEQUALITY ON THE NUMBER LINE

Change $a$, $b$, $c$ and the sign in $a\,x + b \;?\; c$. If $a$ becomes negative, the sign is reversed when you divide.

EXAMPLE 3 · THE SIGN IS REVERSED

Solve $3 - 2x < 11$.

$3 - 2x < 11 \;\big|\; -3 \;\Rightarrow\; -2x < 8 \;\big|\; :(-2)$, the sign is reversed: $x > -4$.

$L = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R} \mid x > -4 \,\}$. Check with $0$: $3 < 11$ is true.

EXAMPLE 4 · WHEN IS TARIFF A CHEAPER?

Tariff A costs $10 + 0.09\,x$ euros, tariff B $0.19\,x$ euros ($x$ in minutes). For which numbers of minutes is A cheaper?

$10 + 0.09\,x < 0.19\,x \;\big|\; -0.09\,x \;\Rightarrow\; 10 < 0.1\,x \;\big|\; :0.1 \;\Rightarrow\; x > 100$.

For more than 100 minutes tariff A is cheaper.

EXERCISES

Solve: a) $x + 4 > 9$   b) $3x \leq 12$   c) $-x > 2$   d) $-4x \geq -20$

a) $x > 5$   b) $x \leq 4$   c) $x < -2$   d) $x \leq 5$

Do $-3$ and $0$ belong to the solution set of $2x + 5 < 0$?

$-3$: $-1 < 0$ true, belongs to it. $0$: $5 < 0$ false, does not belong to it.

Solve and draw the solution set: a) $5x - 3 \geq 2x + 9$   b) $4 - 3x < x + 12$   c) $\tfrac{x - 1}{2} \leq 3$

a) $3x \geq 12$: $x \geq 4$   b) $-4x < 8$: $x > -2$   c) $x - 1 \leq 6$: $x \leq 7$

A van may carry a load of 1.2 t. The driver weighs 80 kg, each box 35 kg. What is the largest number of boxes he may load?

$80 + 35n \leq 1200 \Rightarrow 35n \leq 1120 \Rightarrow n \leq 32$: at most 32 boxes.

For which $x$ does $3 \leq 2x - 1 < 9$ hold? State the solution set. Which integers belong to it?

$4 \leq 2x < 10 \Rightarrow 2 \leq x < 5$, so $L = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R} \mid 2 \leq x < 5 \,\}$. Integers: $2$, $3$, $4$.

TEST YOURSELF!

What is the solution of $-2x > 6$?

Dividing by $-2$ reverses the sign: $x < -3$.

A van can carry 1.2 t and the driver weighs 80 kg. What is the largest number of 35 kg boxes it may load?

$35n \leq 1120$, $n \leq 32$

The solution set of $3 - 2x < 11$ is $\{\, x \mid x > a \,\}$. What is $a$?

$x > -4$, so $a = -4$.

UNIT 32 LESSONS

3Equations with fractions

In one hour pump A manages $\tfrac16$ of the pool, pump B $\tfrac13$. If both together need $x$ hours, they manage $\tfrac1x$ per hour. So $\tfrac16 + \tfrac13 = \tfrac1x$. Multiplied by the common denominator $6x$: $x + 2x = 6$, so $x = 2$ hours, not 4.5.

If the variable is in the denominator, it is called an equation with fractions (a fractional equation). Multiplying by the common denominator turns it into a simple equation. Careful: numbers for which a denominator becomes zero must not be solutions, even if they come out at the end.

KEY POINT · SOLVING EQUATIONS WITH FRACTIONS

1. Determine the domain: exclude all numbers for which a denominator becomes zero.

2. Multiply both sides by the common denominator. 3. Solve the resulting equation.

4. Check whether the solution lies in the domain. If not, it is a false solution and does not belong to $L$.

Why false solutions? When you multiply by the common denominator, you may be multiplying by zero. That is not an equivalence transformation.

Graphically: the solution of $\tfrac{6}{x - 1} = 3$ is the $x$-coordinate of the point of intersection in the picture above: $x = 3$.

PICTURE · BOTH SIDES AS GRAPHS

$\dfrac{3}{x - 2}$ and $\dfrac{5}{x + 2}$ as functions. At $x = 2$ and at $x = -2$ one of the terms is not defined; there the graph jumps. The point of intersection gives the solution of example 5.

EXAMPLE 5 · TWO DENOMINATORS

Solve $\dfrac{3}{x - 2} = \dfrac{5}{x + 2}$.

$D = \mathbb{R} \setminus \{2, -2\}$. Multiply by $(x - 2)(x + 2)$: $3(x + 2) = 5(x - 2)$.

$3x + 6 = 5x - 10 \Rightarrow 16 = 2x \Rightarrow x = 8 \in D$. Check: $\tfrac36 = \tfrac{5}{10}$. $L = \{8\}$

EXAMPLE 6 · A FALSE SOLUTION

Solve $\dfrac{x}{x - 1} = \dfrac{1}{x - 1} + 2$.

$D = \mathbb{R} \setminus \{1\}$. Times $(x - 1)$: $x = 1 + 2(x - 1) = 2x - 1$, so $x = 1$.

But $1 \notin D$: a false solution. $L = \{\,\}$

EXERCISES

State $D$ and solve: a) $\dfrac{12}{x} = 4$   b) $\dfrac{5}{x + 1} = 1$   c) $\dfrac{2}{x - 3} = \dfrac{4}{x + 1}$

a) $D = \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}$, $x = 3$   b) $D = \mathbb{R} \setminus \{-1\}$, $x = 4$   c) $D = \mathbb{R} \setminus \{3, -1\}$: $2(x + 1) = 4(x - 3) \Rightarrow x = 7$

Solve $\dfrac{x + 3}{x - 1} = 2$.

$D = \mathbb{R} \setminus \{1\}$: $x + 3 = 2x - 2 \Rightarrow x = 5 \in D$. $L = \{5\}$

One printer completes a job in 4 hours, a second one in 6 hours. How long do both take together?

$\tfrac14 + \tfrac16 = \tfrac1x \Rightarrow 3x + 2x = 12 \Rightarrow x = 2.4$: 2 hours 24 minutes.

Solve $\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 3} = \dfrac{4}{x - 3}$. What do you notice?

$D = \mathbb{R} \setminus \{3\}$. $x + 1 = 4 \Rightarrow x = 3 \notin D$: a false solution, $L = \{\,\}$.

4 litres of a 30 per cent solution are to be diluted with water to 20%. How much water must be added?

The pure substance stays the same: $0.3 \cdot 4 = 1.2$ litres. The proportion afterwards is $\tfrac{1.2}{4 + x}$.

$\dfrac{1.2}{4 + x} = 0.2 \Rightarrow 1.2 = 0.8 + 0.2\,x \Rightarrow x = 2$: 2 litres of water.

TEST YOURSELF!

Solve $\dfrac{3}{x - 2} = \dfrac{5}{x + 2}$.

$3x + 6 = 5x - 10$, $x = 8$

Which numbers do not belong to the domain of this equation?

Neither denominator may become zero.

Two printers alone need 4 h and 6 h. How many hours do they need together?

$\tfrac{12}{5} = 2.4$ h

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Solve and check: $7 - 2(x - 3) = 3x - 2$

$13 - 2x = 3x - 2 \Rightarrow 15 = 5x \Rightarrow x = 3$. Check: $7 - 0 = 7$ and $9 - 2 = 7$.

Connecting with chapter 1.2: supplier A has €200 fixed costs and €3 per item, supplier B €50 fixed costs and €4.50 per item. From how many items on is A cheaper?

$200 + 3x < 50 + 4.5x \Rightarrow 150 < 1.5x \Rightarrow x > 100$: from 101 items on.

A rectangle is 4 cm longer than it is wide, and its perimeter is at most 40 cm. Which widths are possible?

$2(b + b + 4) \leq 40 \Rightarrow 4b \leq 32 \Rightarrow b \leq 8$. With $b > 0$: $0 < b \leq 8$ (in cm).

For which numbers $a$ does $a\,x + 3 = 2x - 1$ have exactly one solution, no solution or infinitely many solutions?

$(a - 2)\,x = -4$. For $a \neq 2$ exactly one: $x = \tfrac{-4}{a - 2}$. For $a = 2$ we get $0 = -4$: no solution. There are never infinitely many.

EXCURSIONHISTORY

Where the word “algebra” comes from

Around 820 the scholar Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi wrote a textbook on solving equations in Baghdad. In it he names two basic steps: al-ǧabr, “completing”, moves subtracted quantities to the other side, and al-muqābala, “balancing”, cancels equal things on both sides. That is exactly what you do with $\big|\; +3$ and $\big|\; -2x$.

“Al-ǧabr” in the title became “algebra”, and his name became “algorismus” in Latin translations and finally our word algorithm. By the way, al-Khwarizmi did not write formulas; he wrote everything in words.

Source: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi, “al-Kitāb al-muḫtaṣar fī ḥisāb al-ǧabr wa-l-muqābala” (The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing), Baghdad, around 820.

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

EQUIVALENCE TRANSFORMATIONS

Add or subtract the same on both sides, multiply or divide by the same number $\neq 0$.

$3x - 7 = 20 \Rightarrow 3x = 27 \Rightarrow x = 9$

SPECIAL CASES

Contradiction: $L = \{\,\}$. Always true: $L = \mathbb{R}$.

$4x - 1 = 4x + 4$: $L = \{\,\}$

INEQUALITIES

Like equations, but multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the sign.

$-2x < 8 \Rightarrow x > -4$

NUMBER LINE

Half-line, end point filled for $\leq$, $\geq$, open for $<$, $>$.

$L = \{\, x \mid x > -4 \,\}$

EQUATIONS WITH FRACTIONS

First $D$, then multiply by the common denominator, solve, check the solution against $D$.

$\tfrac16 + \tfrac13 = \tfrac1x \Rightarrow x = 2$

$x > 100$, so from 101 items on.

$2x + 2 = 4x - 12$, $x = 7$
